chapter_title: Concerning the Dragon with Fourteen Heads; what it is and [...]
chapter_note: The chapter is largely a systematic microcosm mapping (dragon ↔ bodily faculties/organs; five dens; fourteen heads) in an impersonal expository voice—typical of the older correspondential teaching layer. Paragraphs 1–2 and 9 are dialogue frame (disciple question / apostle response / closing blessing). Paragraph 7 contains a late institutional label sequence (“holy righteous one, elect”) but is embedded in an otherwise core soteriological mechanism; thus treated as MIXED with the institutional titles removed.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Dialogue framing and petition formula (“disciple asked… I beseech you, my master”) plus attribution to the apostle; this is compiling-community apparatus, not the impersonal teaching layer.

paragraphs.core_text: There is never a dragon in the flesh with fourteen heads, as the Magi say! Rather, this is a spiritual lesson. It was uttered in virginity [ ... ] the Magi did not understand [ ... ] all their words that are written [ ... spiri]tual (?).
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed opening dialogue attribution: “Then the apostle says to him:” (frame marker; ‘apostle’ is layer-2 compilation voice).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core doctrinal clarification (not a physical dragon; ‘spiritual lesson’) appears to be the teaching proper; only the speaker-tag is late frame.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, this is how this earth [ ... ] to it, as it is accounted a corporeal dragon [ ... ] I will instruct you [ ... ] the dragon is this doctrine [ ... ] of the flesh [ ... ] also the fourteen heads that are distributed over the dragon are these.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal expository transition into a numbered/structured mapping (“fourteen heads… are these”), characteristic of the older systematic layer.

paragraphs.core_text: The seven sense organs on the head of the body are the two of sight by which one sees; the two of sound by which one hears; the two of scent by which one smells; also the tongue [ ... ] by which one selects, receiving there the different tastes that occur in every form.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Microcosm-correspondence mapping of faculties/organs in enumerated form; no citation or institutional register.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the seven heads of the dragon, the seven sense organs that are on the upper part of the person; [ ... ] below. The seven of the torso are these: two [ ... ]; the two [ ... ] ruler [ ... ] the seven heads that are above; so with the ones below they total and make fourteen heads of the dragon.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continuation of the structural fourteen-fold scheme; systematic counting logic (“total and make fourteen heads”).

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.253⟩
Conversely, the five dens about which they have spoken, where the dragon is congregated and protrudes, are these: the first is the tongue; the second is the lungs; the third is the heart; the fourth is the spleen; the fifth is the blood that dwells in them. Again, if it shall look out from them [and reveal its likeness and its observation above and below, it wages war by] its fourteen heads.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic old teaching style: fixed five-fold list tied to bodily loci + mechanistic description (“wages war by its fourteen heads”). No frame/pastoral cues.

paragraphs.core_text: Whoever will recognise them with the dragon, which is the thought of the body, and struggles with it and is victorious and kills it in them [ ... ] He receives the victory without suffering on the day of his coming forth.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed institutional identity/titles: “he is called] the holy righteous one, elect, good person.” These are community labels rather than the underlying mechanism.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core is the psychophysical mechanism (dragon = thought of the body; struggle/victory; eschatological ‘coming forth’). The inserted naming formula with ‘elect’ reflects later Manichaean institutional vocabulary.

paragraphs.core_text: So, behold, I have taught you of the dragon that exists with its fourteen heads and five dens, wherein it is concealed and hidden. It does through them [ ... / its des]ire all the time.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Teaching-summary closure in expository voice (recap of 14/5 structure, ongoing operation of desire). No explicit hagiographic praise/citation.
Closing dialogue response and blessing formula (“Then that disciple says… Blessed is every one…”), characteristic of the Kephalaia’s editorial frame rather than the older instructional layer.
